### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/spec`, touching **5** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/authorable-surface/api.json`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**1** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/concepts/metadata-lifecycle.mdx`  _(via /packages/:id/export (route, a path literal in a comment on a changed line))_

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/authorable-surface/api.json`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **1** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **60** of **216** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **156** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **156**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **101** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **168** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 0bfb225e4d6b359d8481ec3f5351221c634ed35c` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `36d64618552ec31dbf211f89ebcec16532ae0932` — the merge of head `d558859f50d9e6f3bc0f904bb639334a3572402e` into base `0bfb225e4d6b359d8481ec3f5351221c634ed35c`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 36d64618552ec31dbf211f89ebcec16532ae0932 && git checkout 36d64618552ec31dbf211f89ebcec16532ae0932
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 0bfb225e4d6b359d8481ec3f5351221c634ed35c d558859f50d9e6f3bc0f904bb639334a3572402e && git checkout -B drift-repro 0bfb225e4d6b359d8481ec3f5351221c634ed35c && git merge --no-ff d558859f50d9e6f3bc0f904bb639334a3572402e

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 0bfb225e4d6b359d8481ec3f5351221c634ed35c
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 0bfb225e4d6b359d8481ec3f5351221c634ed35c` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `27e2a7a53f91d227c865a77e4d5b0c4841baf22f`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/api/package-lifecycle.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/kernel/unmanaged-install.ts + packages/spec/src/api/package-lifecycle.test.ts, packages/spec/src/kernel/unmanaged-install.test.ts, .changeset/29373-export-withheld-maps.md, packages/spec/src/integration/connector-credential-redaction.ts (main), packages/runtime/src/domains/packages.ts `assemblePackageManifest` (main), packages/metadata-protocol/src/package-unmanaged-install.ts `planUnmanagedImport` (main), packages/spec/src/stack.zod.ts (the authoring-side reader of the table), packages/spec/src/api/package-api.zod.ts `PackageInstallManifestSchema` (main), packages/cloud-connection/src/marketplace-install-local-plugin.ts `declaredPackageManifest` (main), draft PR #29100 head `1e673873a5ee`

Inputs read: card #29373 body and every comment (triage 6580300184, claim 6582245473, dev report 6583817463, claim amendment 6583855373); #28640 director record 6566912252 (ruling ③A); #29342 dev report 6578135265 and seat ruling 6578196369 (option A); PR #29521 body, 8 files, net diff `origin/main...27e2a7a5`; the head's check-runs. The seat's conclusions were not adopted; each point below was re-read in the tree.

### ① Derived judgments

- **Ruling ③A is honoured by the shape.** `withheldMaps` is a list of `{ type, name, path }` positions, `path` a closed enum, the entry `.strict()` so a `keys: [...]` name list is refused (pinned: "refuses a list of the withheld header names"). No per-entry hiding, no name list. The credential heuristic does not become an export contract: the enum is the redactor's *map* list (`CONNECTOR_CREDENTIAL_MAP_PATHS`, module note item 3), not the `credential-literal` predicate or the URL/query heuristics (items 5 and 6), which stay the redactor's.
- **The closed `path` enum is exactly the redactor's four maps, spelled as it reports them.** Read on main: `CONNECTOR_CREDENTIAL_MAP_PATHS` = `['providerConfig','headers']`, `['providerConfig','defaultHeaders']`, `['providerConfig','transport','headers']`, `['providerConfig','transport','env']`, and `redactConnectorItem` reports `path.join('.')`. The test pins the enum to both the constant and a real redaction's `redactedKeys`, so they cannot drift. The card's three root-less spellings were wrong; the PR's correction is right.
- **The `providerConfig.` root resolves at an import.** The redactor's paths are item-relative (`readAt(item, path)` from the connector body), and an import holds exactly that body (`enumerateItems` in the planner, `manifest[plural]` in the export), so `providerConfig.headers` is the key an import re-enters into; a root-less `headers` would not be.
- **`type: z.literal('connector')` is right for this card.** The seat ruling keeps webhook `headers` (`.meta({ credential: 'map' })`, `automation/webhook.zod.ts:203`) out of scope. A later slot is a literal-to-enum widening on an optional key: `Clause-②: yes (widening)`, no break. Noted, not required: the describe's sentence "a connector's header and environment-variable maps" will need rewording when that slot arrives.
- **`door` for `withheldMaps` opens nothing unintended.** The only two readers of the table are read: `planUnmanagedImport` (`case 'door': break` — nothing reaches `identity`, so nothing reaches `baseManifest`), and `defineStack`'s authoring judge (`stack.zod.ts:2541`), which acts only on `UNMANAGED_INSTALL_REFUSING_DISPOSITIONS`; `door` is not one, so no authoring refusal moves. The base is registered through the closed `PackageInstallManifestSchema` (`ManifestSchema` is `strictObject`), which declares neither key, so carrying either onto the base would refuse the base — `door` is the only disposition that lets an export through without breaking the base.
- **`label` was really refused before.** On main the table has no `label` row and the planner's `default:` arm refuses an unclassified key with `UNMANAGED_INSTALL_UNCOPYABLE` ("not a key a package body declares"), while `assemblePackageManifest` writes `manifest.label` when `pkg.manifest.label ?? pkg.label` is set. The gap is real by reading, independent of the dev's probe. `door` is defensible (see ④ for the reservation).
- **The totality test is sound.** It holds the table total against `ManifestSchema` (live, non-collection), `ObjectStackDefinitionSchema` (non-collection) and now `PackageExportManifestSchema.shape` (the five fixed keys; the catch-all carries the collections, judged by the registry), and the reverse test ("classifies nothing no schema declares") now admits the export's keys so `label` and `withheldMaps` are declared rows, not stale ones. `lazySchema` proxies `.shape` through, so `exportShape` is the real declaration. A sixth fixed key added to the export later reds the spec test on the PR that adds it, as intended.
- **Consumers.** `PackageExportManifest` is the client's `packages.export` return type (`packages/client/src/index.ts:3106`) and the runtime route ledger's `responseSchema` (`route-ledger.ts:547`); an optional key widens both without a break. `api-surface` does not move (inline declaration). The managed install path for an exported body reads the manifest loosely (`declaredPackageManifest(body)` in `marketplace-install-local-plugin.ts:608`, no whole-body strict parse found), and the strict `POST /packages` door takes authoring-stage manifests (`objects` are glob strings), not exports — so no further spec classification is needed for the server half to read `withheldMaps` at the managed door.

### ② Semver level

- `Clause-②: yes (widening)` is right: the unmanaged door's accept set grows by two keys and the export contract gains one optional key; nothing is refused that was accepted before.
- `Metadata-protocol: added` with `'@objectstack/spec': minor` is consistent across the PR body and `.changeset/29373-export-withheld-maps.md`, and matches the precedent pair on main for new API response keys (`28737-record-page-timeline-count.md`, `28722-customizations-contributions.md`: both `yes (widening)` + `added` + spec minor). The gate's own text ties the kind to the moved `authorable-surface/api.json` shard, which this PR moves by one row.
- Check-run reading: the one completed `Check Changeset` on this head is red (job 125437733906, done 2026-11-02T17:34:23Z) because it read the PR body as it stood then — `Metadata-protocol: none` beside the moved shard; the body was amended to `added` at 2026-11-02T17:38:27Z, the 17:37 rerun was cancelled, and a third run (41493231828) was in progress at review time. The tree's changeset already carries `added` + minor, so the red is the body's history, not the tree's — but the record notes that no green `Check Changeset` existed on this head at review time. Landing waits on every check green regardless.

### ③ Boundary flags

- No governed surface in the file list; the review is owed by the published schema face alone (`reviewFace` hits: the two spec source files).
- Spec only: no runtime change; `assemblePackageManifest` does not write the key and no door reads it — the server half is #29342, `pm:blocked` on this card.
- #29100 compatibility: that draft composes `packages: z.array(PackageExportManifestSchema)` by identity in a different hunk (`@@ -191,6 +191,104 @@`, below this PR's edit); the constant's identity is unchanged, so the bundle inherits `withheldMaps` per entry. Git reading on this clone: `git merge-tree --write-tree origin/main 27e2a7a5` is clean (origin/main at `399df5bba8` at review time; the PR was opened on base `04e0c2c0`).
- Generated artifacts in the diff (`content/docs/references/api/package-lifecycle.mdx`, `authorable-surface/api.json`, the strictness-ledger count 487 to 488) read as the regeneration of the one new `.strict()` entry and one new row; not re-run here (read-only), CI's `TypeScript Type Check` lanes are the authority and were in progress at review time.
- Test Core, Build Core, Type Check and the Lint lanes were `in_progress` at review time; only `Spec property liveness`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, `PR-body guards`, `Lint · PM dispatch-gates` and `Lint · scoped · tooling self-tests` had concluded `success`. The record does not claim green.

### ④ Design judgment

- **MUST-FIX — the describe promises a reading of absence that no runtime serves, with no PLANNED marker.** The `withheldMaps` describe ends "Absent when the export withheld nothing." and says "an import reads this list to tell an incomplete map from one the package never had". On this tree the export never writes the key and no import reads it, so today every export that withheld a map has the key absent — the describe's stated meaning of absence is false against the only producer that exists, and it ships into `content/docs/references/api/package-lifecycle.mdx` as the contract. The file's own header says every schema here is a "DESCRIBE-ONLY TRANSCRIPTION of the return type its producer already declares inline" with the named exceptions listed; `withheldMaps` is declared ahead of its producer and is not named among them. The house's own convention for a declaration ahead of its producer, in this same file and by this same seat, is the `[PLANNED — not yet served]` prefix on the describe with a test pinning the marker and the mounting PR dropping it (#29100 `PackageExportBundleSchema`; `ui/app.zod.ts:422`, `view.zod.ts:1217`, `component.zod.ts:1098` for the rendered twin). The changeset's "The export does not write it yet; the runtime half follows" lives only in the changeset, which the reference docs and the client types do not carry. Remedy (small, text-only, same PR): open the describe with `[PLANNED — not yet served]`, state that until the export writes it an absent key says nothing about what was withheld (so an import must not read absence as "nothing withheld" from an exporter predating the key), add that pin to `package-lifecycle.test.ts`, and name the exception in the module header; #29342 drops the marker when it writes the list. Prime Directive #10's corollary (declared ≠ enforced) is the rule this reds against.
- **Reservation, not a must-fix — `label: 'door'` is a silent drop dressed as a door act.** The planner's `door` arm does nothing with `label`; the base takes `targetName ?? name`, and nothing in `ImportUnmanagedPackageResponseSchema` says the display label was set aside (its precedent for "a loss, stated" is `strippedLocks`). The PR widened the `door` definition text to "or, for an export's display `label`, set aside by it" to fit. It closes a real refusal with no new authorable surface, which is the right call for this card, and a display label is low-stakes; but the server half (or the dev's option B card: `label` on the install manifest, classified `identity`) should make the set-aside loud. Recorded so #29342 reads it.
- The `redactedKeys` equality test is a good drift pin, but it only proves the four map positions on a connector carrying all four; it does not (and need not) prove the export's future list matches a given export — that is #29342's test to write.
- Names (`withheldMaps`, `type` / `name` / `path`) are the seat's call per the claim amendment; the ruling's own spelling, accepted as built.

The `Spec property liveness` check-run on `3980d79c` concluded `success` at 2026-11-02T18:06:52Z. The `[PLANNED — not yet served]` marker is the API-schema convention, distinct from the liveness ledger's `[EXPERIMENTAL — not enforced]` describe marker; the `nav` precedent uses the same split.
- **The regenerated reference matches its source.** `content/docs/references/api/package-lifecycle.mdx` gains the header paragraph and the rewritten `withheldMaps` row with the marker, byte-for-sense equal to the docblock and describe at `3980d79c`; `authorable-surface/api.json` and the strictness count are unchanged by the delta (no key moved).
